trial.title: Effects of Magnesium L-Threonate on Sleep, Recovery, and Athletic Performance in Collegiate Athletes

endpoints.measure: Change in Deep Sleep Duration (minutes) from Baseline to Week 4
endpoints.description: Deep (slow-wave) sleep duration will be measured nightly using WHOOP wearable sensors. Average weekly deep sleep duration will be calculated and compared between groups.

endpoints.measure: Change in Heart Rate Variability (HRV) from Baseline to Week 4
endpoints.description: HRV (measured in ms) will be captured nightly via WHOOP device. Weekly averages will be analyzed to assess autonomic recovery across time points.

endpoints.measure: Change in Countermovement Jump Height (cm) from Baseline to Week 4
endpoints.description: Jump height will be assessed using force plate technology.

endpoints.measure: Change in Reaction Time (ms) from Baseline to Week 4
endpoints.description: Reaction time will be measured using a standardized light-based reaction test (e.g., BlazePod). Group differences will be analyzed after 4 weeks of supplementation.

endpoints.measure: Change in Handgrip Strength from Baseline to Week 4
endpoints.description: Grip strength will be measured using a calibrated handheld dynamometer. The average value from three trials on the dominant hand will be recorded and analyzed.

endpoints.measure: Change in Subjective Sleep Quality Score from Baseline to Week 4
endpoints.description: Participants will complete a Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale (rated 0-10) each morning via REDCap. Weekly averages will be used to assess within- and between-group changes.

analysis_trace.finding: NCT07015047 is a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial of magnesium L-threonate (1g nightly) vs placebo in 100 UCLA varsity athletes over 4 weeks. Primary outcomes: deep sleep duration and HRV via WHOOP. Secondary: jump height, reaction time, grip strength, subjective sleep quality.
Healthy collegiate athletes aged 18-35, actively training, excluded if using sleep meds or magnesium supplements. High-performance population with potentially ceiling effects for some measures.

Mg L-threonate crosses blood-brain barrier, enhances GABAergic tone, reduces glutamate excitotoxicity, supports NMDA receptor function. Mechanistically plausible for sleep architecture and cognitive outcomes; less clear for peripheral performance metrics.

Primary-0 (deep sleep): Direct evidence from HERO Lab AMSSM 2026 poster shows +54.6 min total sleep time at week 2 (p=0.002), +45.5 min at week 4 (p=0.006), and +6.27 pts WHOOP sleep score. Deep sleep specifically not quantified but directionally supported. Evidence_role: direct_numeric for total sleep, indirect_direction for deep sleep specifically. Primary-1 (HRV): Lopresti 2026 (Front Nutr) showed HRV increase (p=0.036) with MgT in adults with poor sleep. Evidence_role: indirect_direction (different population, similar mechanism). Secondary-0 (jump): No pooled benefit expected; AMSSM poster notes no grip strength benefit, suggesting limited peripheral performance effect. Evidence_role: mechanism_background. Secondary-1 (reaction time): AMSSM poster shows -52.3 ms faster reaction time (p=0.001). Evidence_role: direct_numeric. Secondary-2 (grip strength): AMSSM poster explicitly states 'No pooled between-group benefit observed for grip strength.' Evidence_role: direct_numeric (null result). Secondary-3 (sleep quality): AMSSM poster shows +0.83 pts subjective sleep quality in endurance subgroup (p=0.030). Evidence_role: direct_numeric.
MgT generally well-tolerated. Lopresti 2026 reported no significant adverse reactions. Expected AE profile: mild GI symptoms, drowsiness. No serious safety concerns anticipated at 1g nightly dose.

Primary risks: (1) Ceiling effects in healthy young athletes may attenuate sleep/performance benefits vs deficient populations. (2) WHOOP device validity for sleep staging vs polysomnography. (3) Single-blind design may introduce performance bias. (4) 4-week duration may be insufficient for peripheral performance adaptations.

Direct evidence from same trial (AMSSM 2026 poster) supports positive effects on total sleep time, sleep score, reaction time, and subjective sleep quality in subgroups. Null result for grip strength. HRV supported by related trial (Lopresti 2026). Jump height lacks direct evidence. Deep sleep specifically not reported but total sleep improvements suggest likely directional benefit.

No published peer-reviewed results for NCT07015047 as of cutoff. Reliance on conference poster (AMSSM 2026) for primary data. Deep sleep duration specifically not quantified in available sources. HRV data from different population (general adults vs athletes).
